jobs.prompt:
chore(cpp): integrate the ICU, llhttp server and small-helpers library branches into one green branch (stage 1)

CONTEXT (you have no other context than this prompt and the repository)
You start from branch `agent-jobs/cppgw-std-small-helpers-r1-44202204674-1` of ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi: a known-good state of `cpp/gateway/`, a C++20 port of this repository's TypeScript gateway (`src/`, `serve.ts`), with a JavaScript-style runtime layer (`include/uos/rt`, `src/rt`, `src/runtime`), vendored simdjson and simdutf (`cpp/gateway/third_party/`), ICU for Unicode, and about 442 standalone test binaries (`cpp/gateway/tests/**/*_test.cpp`). On this state the release build passes its whole suite on Linux ARM64. The native gateway is already 1.2-1.9x faster than the TypeScript gateway on Bun end to end and uses about a third of the memory (`cpp/gateway/docs/findings/cppgw-perf-request-path-20261117.md`). Every deployment target is 64-bit ARM: an Arch Linux ARM VPS, an Apple Silicon Mac and a Raspberry Pi.

OWNER POLICY (binding): generic functionality comes from mature open-source or standard libraries; exact parity with Bun's quirks and error wording is NOT required; less first-party code is preferred. What must hold: the gateway's functional behaviour (wire formats, status codes, stored data, authentication and validation decisions, accounting) and security never getting weaker.

READ FIRST: `cpp/gateway/docs/CI.md` (portable build-and-test driver; invoke it as `bash cpp/gateway/tools/ci-build.sh ...`, the file lacks its executable bit), `cpp/gateway/docs/BUILD.md`, `cpp/gateway/docs/RUNTIME.md`, `cpp/gateway/docs/OSS-REPLACEMENT-PLAN.md`, `cpp/gateway/PORTING.md` (its coroutine rules are mandatory; its "Host safety" and "compile only through tools/unit.sh" rules apply to the authors' server, not to your disposable runner; where it demands exact Bun parity, the owner policy above wins). `python3 cpp/gateway/tools/links.py <test>` prints a test's application sources; every `src/rt/*.cpp` and the vendored libraries link into every test.

About ten other agents are changing other parts of `cpp/gateway` on their own branches at the same time (URL, HTTP parsing, regex, WebSocket, passkey CBOR and ASN.1, BigInt, date/console/filesystem/env/headers helpers, the stored-value reader, a test-suite repair). You are the INTEGRATOR for the first group of finished branches (see TASK); other lanes are still running and will be integrated on top of your result later, so keep your own edits to what integration needs.

GENERAL RULES
- The runner holds a model gateway token: never print it or write any credential to a file. Run tests with an empty `HOME`, a fresh `TMPDIR` and no provider variables. No real provider traffic: use local mocks only.
- Do not edit `.github/` (unless your task says so), the TypeScript, or `cpp/` outside `cpp/gateway/`. Do not delete or weaken tests.
- Model connections can drop: create your report file in the first minutes and commit small steps often (the tree must build at each commit). Leave no build output, binaries or downloads in the checkout.
- Report file: `cpp/gateway/docs/findings/<job id>.md`: what you did, exact commands, real counts and measurements, what is unfinished, defects found outside your paths (report, do not fix). End your final message with the same summary.

YOUR MACHINE: GitHub-hosted Linux ARM64 runner (Ubuntu 24.04, 4 CPUs, 16 GB, sudo, network). Its packages are too old for this tree: install Clang 21 or newer from apt.llvm.org (or GCC 14+), build Boost 1.92.0 `json` and `container` static libraries from the official source archive in a temp directory (the tree needs Boost >= 1.86), install OpenSSL 3, zlib, ICU, brotli, zstd development packages and build SQLite 3.54.0 as `cpp/gateway/docs/CI.md` describes. Bun 1.4.0 may be installed when you need to run the TypeScript.

OWNED PATHS
- anything under `cpp/gateway/` that the integration needs. Not `.github/`, not the TypeScript, not vendored sources under `cpp/gateway/third_party/` (they stay byte-identical to what the branches vendored).

TASK
You start from `agent-jobs/cppgw-std-small-helpers-r1-44202204674-1` (date, console, filesystem/path, environment and Headers helpers moved to the standard library; report `cpp/gateway/docs/findings/cppgw-std-small-helpers-20261117.md`). Merge these two reviewed and accepted branches into it with ordinary `git merge` commits (fetch them from `origin`):
  1. `agent-jobs/cppgw-std-icu-20261117-44188151110-1`: Unicode case mapping and collation on ICU (`src/rt/string.cpp` lost about 1,450 lines; report `docs/findings/cppgw-std-icu-20261117.md`).
  2. `agent-jobs/cppgw-std-llhttp-server-r1-44202666506-1`: server request-head and chunked-body parsing on llhttp 9.4.4, vendored under `third_party/llhttp/` (report `docs/findings/cppgw-std-llhttp-server-20261117.md`).
Resolve conflicts keeping each branch's intent (expected only in shared registries: `fuzz/targets.json`, `docs/DEVIATIONS-FROM-BUN.md`, `CMakeLists.txt`, `tools/vendor_sources.py`, `cmake/vendors.json`, `tests/LINKS.txt`). Then make the result build and pass:
  a. Register llhttp everywhere a vendored library must be registered so that EVERY build path works: CMake, `tools/vendor_sources.py`, `cmake/vendors.json`, and the portable CI driver (`cmake/ci/driver.py`: the llhttp branch's report says the non-CMake drivers still lack multi-file C archive support; add it, C sources compiled with the C compiler and without the port's warning set).
  b. Each branch's report lists a few tests it could not touch because they were outside its paths. Resolve each one under the owner policy, one commit per test, with the reason in the commit message: the tracked HTTP wire fixture has four Bun-specific expectations (llhttp is stricter or words errors differently): update them if, and only if, the new behaviour is standard-conformant and no real client depends on the old one; three application cases still expect Bun's legacy date parsing or Headers error text: for the date ones, FIRST establish which date formats the gateway really receives (grep the TypeScript and C++ for where provider headers and bodies are parsed into dates: `Retry-After`, rate-limit reset headers, token expiry fields, RFC 1123 HTTP dates, ISO 8601, epoch seconds and milliseconds) and make sure every such format still parses correctly, adding the missing format to the date code if needed; only then change expectations that concern formats nothing sends. A URL/IDNA test that depended on the runner's ICU version: make it pass with the ICU the build actually links (state the version).
  c. Run the whole suite with the driver, release configuration, all shards, and the `asan` configuration for the components these branches touched, until everything is green on your ARM64 runner.
Write `cpp/gateway/docs/findings/cppgw-integrate-s1-20261118.md`: merge order, each conflict and how it was resolved, each test decision with its justification, final counts per shard, first-party production lines in `src/rt` + `src/runtime` before (at commit 55afcc8b1) and after.

DONE WHEN
`bash cpp/gateway/tools/ci-build.sh --config release --shard N/4` passes for N = 1..4 with zero failing binaries on your ARM64 runner, `git log` shows the two merges, and the report is complete. The maintainer will base the next integration stage on your branch.
